title: SecOps-NG Effectiveness Evidence Artifact
description: Typed shape for one evidence artifact emitted by the effectiveness evidence stream (F-CP-06). One artifact is produced per (metric, policy-or-prompt-version, evaluation-window) snapshot and pins, mechanically, the value an effectiveness indicator took at evaluation time, against the specific policy version or prompt version the workflow was operating under, with a pointer to the source-data shape (typically an OCSF class_uid) the indicator was derived from. Downstream consumers are the NIS2 Article 21(2)(f) effectiveness-of-risk-management-measures mapping, kri.control_effectiveness@v1 and its KPI-family siblings, and the F-WF-09 auditor-bundle that reads effectiveness snapshots as the operator-side trail for periodic re-assessment. Public-bar artifact: operator-side strings (policy versions, prompt versions, owner labels) MUST stay role-shaped; individual personal names, credential-shaped strings, and raw measurement payloads carrying personal data are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected at the schema boundary.

schema_version.description: Pinned schema version. Lets a consumer reject artifacts produced under an older schema once breaking changes ship.

artifact_id.description: Stable per-artifact identifier. Convention: SHA-256 hex digest of `<workflow_id>|<execution_id>|<compile_target>|<metric_ref>|<subject_version.value>` (UTF-8, no separators around the pipes). Deterministic on those five inputs so a replay of the same evaluation under the same compile target re-derives the same id; re-emissions inside the same execution stay byte-identical at the path level.

stream.description: Identifies which evidence stream produced the artifact. Constant on this schema.

workflow_id.description: Stable identifier of the workflow whose execution produced this effectiveness snapshot. Convention: lower-snake-case workflow stable-id from `content/playbooks/<workflow>/` (e.g. `incident_management`, `vulnerability_triage`). Joins back into the workflow content layer so a reviewer can re-derive which playbook was compiled into the running form.

execution_id.description: Per-execution identifier issued by the compile target's workflow runtime (n8n execution id, Temporal workflow run id, LangGraph thread/checkpoint id). Each evaluation emits its own snapshot — re-runs of the same workflow produce distinct execution_ids and distinct artifact_ids.

compile_target.description: Which of the three reference compile targets produced the running form of the workflow. The snapshot is target-specific because the runtime that evaluated the metric is target-specific. Constrained to the three reference targets the project ships compilers for; community-contributed targets are out of scope for this enum.

regulation_refs.description: Pins to the upstream regulatory mapping entries this snapshot helps satisfy (typically `nis2:art-21-2-f`). At least one entry — a snapshot with no regulatory anchor is not evidence in the F-CP-06 sense. Joins back into content/mappings/<regime>/*.yaml via the `id` field.

control_refs.description: Control stable-ids attested by this snapshot. Same shape every other layer of the content model uses. At least one — typically `control.control_effectiveness_test@v1` plus whichever risk-management control the indicator measures.

metric_ref.description: Stable id of the KPI or KRI this snapshot is a measurement of. Reuses the `kpi.<slug>@v<semver>` / `kri.<slug>@v<semver>` namespace declared by content/metrics/*.yaml — the reference shape for the F-CP-06 stream is `kri.control_effectiveness@v1`, but the artifact accepts any kpi/kri stable-id so downstream catalogue growth does not require a schema bump.

subject_version.description: The thing whose effectiveness this snapshot measures, pinned to a specific version. Two `kind` values are supported: `policy_version` for policy text / OSCAL component / control attestation versions (semver-shaped or content-hash), and `prompt_version` for prompt-anchored agentic workflow surfaces (semver-shaped or content-hash). A snapshot has exactly one subject version; mixed-subject rollups are out of scope at this layer.

kind.description: Mechanical classification of what is being versioned. `policy_version` is the operator-side risk-management-policy surface; `prompt_version` is the prompt-anchored agentic-workflow surface (DSPy / LangGraph prompt). The two are kept distinct because they re-version on different cadences and a reviewer needs to see which surface a movement in the indicator is attributable to.

value.description: Semver-shaped value (e.g. `1.2.0`) or a 64-hex content-hash. The pattern accepts both shapes — the deterministic-id derivation pins on this string verbatim, so emitter conventions are reviewable at the artifact level.

measurement.description: The measured value of the indicator at evaluation time, with its unit, direction, and a pointer to the source-data shape it was derived from (typically an OCSF class_uid). The pre-computed value is the snapshot — the framework deliberately does not embed the underlying sample payload here, because the sample may carry personal data and the source-shape pointer is the public-bar-safe surface a reviewer needs.

value.description: Numeric value the indicator took at evaluation time. Ratios are in the closed interval [0, 1] per the unit; counts are non-negative integers represented as numbers.

unit.description: Unit of the value, drawn from the closed vocabulary content/metrics/*.yaml `unit` declares. `ratio` for normalised [0, 1] values, `count` for non-negative integer counts, `duration_seconds` for elapsed-time measurements, `percent` for [0, 100] percentage values. New units are a discussion at the metric-catalogue layer, not a drive-by schema change.

direction.description: Which direction is better, reused verbatim from the metric-catalogue `direction` field. Carried on the snapshot so a downstream consumer can render the indicator without re-walking the catalogue.

evaluation_window.description: Optional ISO-8601 duration the indicator was evaluated over. Mirrors the catalogue's `measurement.window.duration` for sliding evaluations; omit for point-in-time evaluations.

threshold_crossed.description: Optional name of the threshold the snapshot crossed (`warn`, `breach`, `critical`), drawn from the catalogue's `thresholds[].name`. Carried so downstream rollups skip re-derivation. Reviewer-side correctness check, not schema-enforced beyond the lowercase token shape.

source_shape.description: Pointer to the source-data shape the indicator was derived from. Typically an OCSF event class (`class_uid` and `class_name`); the snapshot carries the pointer, not the underlying sample. Personal data in the underlying sample is out of scope for the snapshot per AGENTS.md §3.

kind.description: Which source-shape vocabulary the pointer reads against. `ocsf` for OCSF event-class identifiers; `telemetry` for the framework's own `telemetry.<slug>@v<semver>` long-form URN; `none` for indicators derived from operator control catalogue state with no external source-data shape.

ocsf.description: OCSF event-class pointer. Required when `kind == ocsf`; rejected otherwise. `class_uid` is a non-negative integer; `class_name` is human-readable; `ocsf_version` is semver-shaped.

telemetry_ref.description: Long-form telemetry URN. Required when `kind == telemetry`; rejected otherwise.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp at which this snapshot was captured. Not part of `artifact_id` — re-emissions inside the same execution stay byte-identical at the path level.

provenance.description: Where this snapshot came from. Mirrors the provenance pattern used by content/controls/*.yaml so a reviewer can re-derive the chain back to source.

source_url.description: URL of the workflow run (or workflow-content source) that produced this snapshot. Compile targets may use their own run-id URLs; the URL itself is opaque to this schema.

captured_at.description: ISO-8601 date or date-time matching the artifact-level captured_at.

commit_sha.description: Optional commit SHA of the content snapshot the workflow walked.

owner.description: Optional dated ownership pointer for the effectiveness posture this snapshot covers. Role-shaped — a working-group mailbox, a generic role title, or a community handle. Individual personal names are out of scope per AGENTS.md §3 and rejected here as a matter of schema discipline. Optional at this layer because the F-CP-06 snapshot is a per-evaluation mechanical measurement; the owning role typically lives on the upstream `control.control_effectiveness_test@v1` entry.

role.description: Generic role or working-group identifier (e.g. 'metrics-wg', 'effectiveness-review-board@example.org'). Personal names are not used.

assigned_at.description: ISO-8601 date on which the role was assigned ownership of the effectiveness posture.

retention.description: Optional retention pointer the operator declares for this evidentiary record. ISO-8601 duration, defaulted by the operator's configuration.
